title: Finiteness of algebraic derived Hom over a finite ring
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring whose underlying set is finite. Let $E,G$ be cochain complexes of $B$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with finite underlying sets in every degree and with terms zero outside bounded intervals of integers. Then the set $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$ is finite.

source.place: Tags 094G lemma-locally-constant, 09BE lemma-locally-constant-map, and 08FR lemma-local-actual; Finiteness of algebraic derived Hom over a finite ring

proof.text: The cycles of a complex with finite terms inject into a finite term, and its homology is a quotient of its cycles, hence finite. A mapping cone from a finite free complex to E has finite terms, so it satisfies the finite-cone hypothesis of the finite-free-model theorem. Obtain a bounded-above complex P of finite free modules and a quasi-isomorphism P to E.

A bounded-above complex of projective modules is K-projective. Every derived map P to G therefore has a representative chain map, using Qh_map_bijective followed by surjectivity of the homotopy quotient on morphisms.

Only the finitely many degrees in a bounded support interval of G can contribute to a chain map. Evaluation in these degrees injects the set of chain maps into a finite product of finite sets of module maps. Outside the interval every map to the zero target is unique. Hence chain maps, and their surjective image of derived maps, form finite sets. The quasi-isomorphism P to E transports this finiteness to Hom(E,G).

theorem finite_derived_hom_of_bounded_finite
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Finite B]
    (E G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ)
    (hE : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E.X n))
    (hG : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hEfin : ∀ n : ℤ, Finite (E.X n)) (hGfin : ∀ n : ℤ, Finite (G.X n)) :
    Finite (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)
